answer: Each task is bound to an anchor and a future threshold-BLS beacon pulse: only after the pulse is finalized is a domain-separated challenge derived, so its unpredictable randomness blocks advance solving, cached-response reuse, and offline farming across fabricated identities. A commit–reveal audit ties each response to that challenge and its deadline; it raises the cost of Sybil swarms rather than treating the beacon itself as proof of one person, while task variants wander across the input space.
